intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Snorkeling & Island Hopping Tour
experiences.description: Embark on a full-day speedboat tour around the stunning Phi Phi archipelago, snorkeling in crystal-clear waters at Maya Bay, exploring Viking Cave, and swimming at Monkey Beach. One of Thailand's most iconic island-hopping experiences with breathtaking limestone karst scenery.

experiences.name: Bangkok Street Food Night Market Tour
experiences.description: Dive deep into Bangkok's legendary street food scene with a guided evening walk through Yaowarat (Chinatown) and Silom. Sample pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay, boat noodles, and fresh coconut ice cream from legendary local vendors that have perfected their recipes over generations.

experiences.name: Railay Beach Rock Climbing & Sunset Exploration
experiences.description: Accessible only by longtail boat, Railay Beach is a secluded paradise surrounded by dramatic limestone cliffs. Spend the day rock climbing with a certified guide, swimming in turquoise waters, and exploring the hidden lagoon before watching one of Thailand's most spectacular sunsets from the beach.

experiences.name: Koh Samui to Koh Tao Multi-Island Ferry Hop
experiences.description: Island-hop through the Gulf of Thailand's gem trio — Koh Samui, Koh Phangan, and Koh Tao. Enjoy world-class snorkeling at Sail Rock, relax on the pristine white sands of Haad Rin Beach, and explore the vibrant coral reefs around Koh Tao, one of the world's top affordable dive destinations.
experiences.location: Koh Samui, Koh Phangan & Koh Tao, Surat Thani Province

experiences.name: Chiang Mai Street Food & Night Bazaar Experience
experiences.description: Wander through Chiang Mai's famous Saturday Walking Street and Night Bazaar, tasting Northern Thai specialties like khao soi (coconut curry noodles), sai oua (herbed sausage), and crispy pork rinds. Interact with local vendors, browse handcrafted goods, and soak in the cultural atmosphere of the ancient Lanna Kingdom city.
experiences.location: Wualai Walking Street & Night Bazaar, Chiang Mai

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, exchange some currency at the airport (avoid hotel exchange rates). Take the Airport Rail Link or a metered taxi to your accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in and settle into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack from a 7-Eleven or nearby street food stall near the resort (pad kra pao or grilled skewers for under 60 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Budget tip: Use the Airport Rail Link (45 THB) instead of taxis to save money. Get a local SIM card at the airport (around 299 THB for 30 days of data). Keep 1000–2000 THB in small bills for street food and tuk-tuks.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and take your first walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Explore the surrounding beach area, watch the morning fishing boats, and get oriented with the local neighborhood. Visit a nearby morning market to sample fresh tropical fruits and local breakfast items.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or motorbike (150–300 THB/day) and explore the local area around the resort. Visit a nearby temple (wat) for free cultural immersion. Explore local streets and scout out the best street food stalls for the coming days.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the nearest beach promenade or night market. Browse stalls, try local snacks, and watch the sunset over the water. Enjoy a relaxed first full evening soaking in the Thai beach atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Local morning market near the resort — rice porridge (jok) or fried dough sticks (patongko) with Thai iced tea, around 60–80 THB
meals.lunch: Street food pad thai or fried rice from a local vendor, 60–80 THB
meals.dinner: Night market dinner — mix of grilled corn, mango sticky rice, som tum (papaya salad), and grilled pork skewers, around 150–200 THB total

day_by_day.notes: Recovery day after travel — keep it easy and low-key. Stay hydrated and use sunscreen. October can bring occasional rain showers, so pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to a local fishing village near the resort. Watch fishermen bring in their catch and interact with locals. Take photos of colorful longtail boats docked along the shore. This is a great free cultural experience unique to coastal Thailand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest popular beach. Rent a snorkel set (100–150 THB) and explore the shallow reef areas. Alternatively, join a budget group snorkeling day trip (500–800 THB) that departs from the main pier and visits 2–3 nearby snorkel spots.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and visit a beachside casual restaurant for sunset drinks. Try a fresh coconut (40–60 THB) while watching the sun go down. Stroll the beach in the evening and enjoy the cooler temperatures.

meals.breakfast: Resort area café or street stall — banana pancake and fruit smoothie, around 80–100 THB
meals.lunch: Beach shack lunch — grilled fish with steamed rice and vegetables, around 120–150 THB
meals.dinner: Local Thai restaurant near the resort — green curry with rice or massaman curry, around 100–150 THB

day_by_day.notes: Book group snorkeling tours at the pier or through guesthouses rather than resort tour desks to get the best budget rates. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day island hopping adventure! Book a budget group speedboat or longtail boat tour (600–1000 THB) departing early morning. Visit 3–4 smaller uninhabited or lightly visited islands in the area, including stops for swimming and snorkeling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island hopping tour. Explore hidden lagoons, limestone karst formations, and pristine beaches only accessible by boat. Enjoy a packed lunch on a secluded beach included in most group tours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the mainland by late afternoon. Rest at the resort, rinse off, and head out for a street food dinner walk. Try dishes you haven't sampled yet — look for boat noodles, larb, or khao man gai.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the tour — toast with egg from a street stall, 50–70 THB
meals.lunch: Packed lunch included in the island hopping tour, or buy from a beach vendor on one of the islands (100–150 THB if not included)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner walk — mix of dishes from multiple stalls totaling 150–200 THB

day_by_day.notes: Book island hopping tours the day before to secure a spot and sometimes negotiate a better price. Bring waterproof bags for your phone and valuables. October weather may cause occasional cancellations — have a backup plan.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local fresh market in the morning for a true Thai experience. Sample exotic fruits like rambutan, mangosteen, and dragon fruit (20–50 THB each). Pick up snacks for the day and practice bargaining in a friendly way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby national park or nature trail on foot or by rented motorbike. Look for viewpoints overlooking the sea and islands. Many national parks charge a small entry fee (200 THB for foreigners) but offer stunning scenery and wildlife spotting.
day_by_day.evening: Join a Thai cooking class (budget options available for 500–800 THB) where you learn to make 3–4 classic dishes like tom yum soup, pad thai, and green curry. This doubles as your dinner for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Fresh market fruits and local snacks, around 80–100 THB
meals.lunch: National park or viewpoint area food stall — fried rice or noodle soup, 80–100 THB
meals.dinner: Thai cooking class meal — you cook and eat your own creations (included in class fee)

day_by_day.notes: Budget cooking classes can be found at local guesthouses or community centers — avoid resort-branded classes which charge double. Check TripAdvisor or ask fellow travelers for recommendations.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry or speedboat to a nearby famous island for a day trip or overnight stay. Popular budget-friendly islands in Thailand include Koh Lanta, Koh Phangan, Koh Tao, or Koh Chang depending on your resort's location. Depart early to maximize time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island on foot or rent a motorbike (150–200 THB/day). Visit the island's main beach, a local temple, and a viewpoint. Swim in crystal-clear waters and relax on white sand beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from a clifftop bar or beachside spot. Enjoy the island's night atmosphere — many islands have lively but affordable beach bars and night markets. Try a bucket cocktail (local tradition) for 150–200 THB.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before ferry departure — fruit and coffee from a street stall, 60–80 THB
meals.lunch: Island beachside restaurant — fresh seafood platter or grilled fish with rice, 150–200 THB
meals.dinner: Island night market or beach restaurant — pad thai, spring rolls, and fresh fruit shake, around 150–180 THB

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets vary by destination — book in advance during peak season. Budget guesthouses on most Thai islands run 300–600 THB per night if you decide to stay overnight. Keep your resort booking in mind for the return.

day_by_day.morning: If you stayed overnight on the island, explore quieter beaches and hidden coves in the early morning before the crowds arrive. Rent a kayak (150–200 THB/hour) to explore sea caves or mangrove channels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return by ferry to your home base at Aegean Bliss Resort. Freshen up and take a leisurely afternoon swim at the resort's beachfront. Visit a nearby spa for a budget Thai massage (200–350 THB for 1 hour) — a midweek treat.
day_by_day.evening: Relax evening at the resort area. Visit a beachfront casual restaurant and try a seafood barbecue — many Thai beach restaurants let you pick fresh seafood by weight and grill it to order at reasonable prices.

meals.breakfast: Island guesthouse breakfast or street stall near the ferry pier — fried egg on rice, 60–80 THB
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite on the ferry or at the pier — snacks and drinks, 80–100 THB
meals.dinner: Beachfront seafood BBQ — grilled prawns, squid, and fish with sticky rice and som tum, around 250–350 THB

day_by_day.notes: Thai massage is excellent value and great for sore muscles after active days. Look for local massage shops on side streets rather than resort spas — same quality at half the price.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a famous local Buddhist temple (wat) in the region. Dress respectfully (cover shoulders and knees — bring a sarong). Explore the temple grounds, observe monks during morning prayers, and learn about Thai Buddhist culture. Entry is usually free or minimal donation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby town or village by songthaew (shared red truck taxi, 20–40 THB per ride). Visit a local market, browse handicraft shops, and look for budget souvenirs like elephant pants, wooden carvings, and handmade jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Find a local restaurant away from tourist areas for an authentic dinner. Ask locals or guesthouse staff for recommendations — these hidden gems offer the best food at the lowest prices. Try khao pad sapparod (pineapple fried rice) or tom kha gai (coconut soup).

meals.breakfast: Thai-style breakfast at a local coffee shop — toast with kaya jam, soft-boiled eggs, and Thai iced coffee, around 80–100 THB
meals.lunch: Local market lunch — a selection of pre-made dishes served over rice, 60–80 THB
meals.dinner: Local neighborhood restaurant — 2–3 dishes shared family style with steamed rice, around 200–250 THB for two

day_by_day.notes: Cultural day — be mindful of temple etiquette. Remove shoes before entering temple buildings. Avoid touching Buddha statues or monks. Photography is usually allowed outside but ask inside.

day_by_day.morning: Second major island hopping excursion — this time targeting different islands or a longer route. Book a full-day longtail boat private charter with a group (split cost with other travelers, 800–1200 THB per person) for a more personalized experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a famous landmark like a sea cave, floating village, or James Bond Island-style karst formation depending on your region. Snorkel over coral gardens and look for tropical fish, sea turtles, and starfish.
day_by_day.evening: Beach bonfire or fire show evening — many Thai beach resorts and bars host fire shows and beach parties. Enjoy the atmosphere with a local beer (Chang or Singha, 60–80 THB) and street food snacks.

meals.breakfast: Early departure breakfast — convenience store items or quick street stall, 60–80 THB
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the boat or beach BBQ at a secluded island stop, 100–150 THB
meals.dinner: Beach bar dinner — grilled chicken satay, spring rolls, and fried noodles, around 200 THB

day_by_day.notes: Always check weather forecasts before boat trips. October can have afternoon rain squalls. Responsible operators will cancel in unsafe conditions and offer refunds or rescheduling.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga or meditation on the beach (many resorts and local studios offer free or donation-based morning sessions). Spend the morning relaxing on the beach, reading, or journaling. A well-deserved slow morning after active days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local waterfall or inland natural attraction accessible by motorbike. Many Thai coastal regions have beautiful waterfalls within 30–60 minutes of the beach. Swim in natural pools and enjoy the jungle scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Street food tour — dedicate the evening to systematically trying as many different street foods as possible. Set a budget of 200 THB and see how many dishes you can sample: satay sticks, grilled corn, mango sticky rice, roti, fresh spring rolls, and more.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or açaí bowl from a health café near the beach (increasingly popular in Thai beach towns), around 120–150 THB
meals.lunch: Waterfall area food stall or pack your own picnic from the morning market, 80–120 THB
meals.dinner: Street food tour budget of 200 THB — sample 6–8 different items from various stalls

day_by_day.notes: Motorbike rental tip: Always inspect the bike before renting and photograph any existing damage. Wear a helmet — it's the law and it's safe. International driving permit is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local fishing pier early morning to see the daily catch being unloaded and sold. This is one of the most authentic and photogenic experiences in coastal Thailand. Buy fresh seafood directly from fishermen at very low prices if you have cooking facilities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a different beach or bay you haven't visited yet. Many Thai coastal areas have multiple beaches with very different characters — some busy and lively, others quiet and secluded. Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Thai cultural show or Muay Thai boxing match if available locally (200–400 THB for local venues vs. 1000+ THB at tourist venues). This is an exciting and authentic cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Fishing pier area breakfast — fresh seafood congee or fish soup, around 80–100 THB
meals.lunch: Beach food stall — fresh coconut, grilled seafood, and papaya salad, around 150 THB
meals.dinner: Near the cultural show venue — street food or casual restaurant, around 150–200 THB

day_by_day.notes: For Muay Thai, look for local training camp fights rather than tourist stadium shows — far cheaper, more authentic, and you're supporting local fighters directly.

day_by_day.morning: Final island or beach excursion — revisit your favorite spot from the trip or explore one last new location. Spend the morning doing your favorite activity from the past two weeks, whether that's snorkeling, kayaking, or simply relaxing on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping and last-minute exploration. Visit local markets for gifts: Thai silk scarves (200–400 THB), spice sets (100–200 THB), elephant figurines, and handmade crafts. Practice your bargaining skills one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best local restaurant you discovered during the trip. Treat yourself slightly — order a few extra dishes to try things you haven't had yet. Reflect on the trip over a cold Singha beer or fresh fruit shake.

meals.breakfast: Favorite breakfast spot from the trip — revisit the best morning meal you had
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the markets — noodle soup or fried rice, 80–100 THB
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at the best local restaurant discovered during the trip — budget 300–400 THB for a slightly elevated final meal

day_by_day.notes: Pack souvenirs carefully — liquid items like fish sauce or coconut oil must go in checked luggage. Dried spices and sealed food items are generally fine in carry-on. Keep receipts for customs if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk on the beach. Take photos, collect a few shells as free souvenirs, and say goodbye to the ocean. Enjoy a leisurely final breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort (most checkouts are by 12:00 noon — arrange luggage storage if your flight is later). Head to the airport with plenty of time — allow at least 3 hours for international flights. Take the most budget-friendly transport option available.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Thailand. At the airport, use remaining Thai baht on airport food or duty-free items. Reflect on 13 incredible days of beaches, island hopping, and street food adventures across one of the world's most beautiful countries.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — khao tom (rice soup) or fried eggs with toast and Thai iced tea, around 80–100 THB
meals.lunch: Airport food court — surprisingly affordable with local Thai options available, around 150–200 THB
meals.dinner: On the plane or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tip: A well-managed 13-day budget Thailand trip should cost approximately 15,000–25,000 THB (roughly $400–$700 USD) excluding flights, covering accommodation supplements, food, activities, and transport. Keep 500 THB aside for airport departure tax if not included in your ticket.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi Airport on Flight UA at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange private transfer or airport taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Skip — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Skip — in-flight meal
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack at the airport's food court (Try boat noodles or pad kra pao at one of the 24-hour stalls, ~150-250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Thai Baht handy for taxi or tips. Pre-book airport transfer if possible to avoid hassle at midnight. Confirm hotel night check-in arrangements in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow stroll along the beachfront to get oriented with your surroundings and enjoy the morning sea breeze.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate beach area around the resort. Rent a beach chair and umbrella, take a swim in the warm Gulf of Thailand waters, and browse nearby beachside shops for sunscreen, snacks, and souvenirs. Visit a local convenience store to stock up on essentials.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the nearest beach town's night market for your first proper Thai street food experience. Try grilled satay skewers, mango sticky rice, and fresh coconut ice cream while soaking in the lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or à la carte — enjoy tropical fruits, congee, and Thai-style eggs (~200-350 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside casual restaurant — try a classic Pad Thai or green curry with rice (~150-250 THB)
meals.dinner: Local night market street food spread — satay, som tum (papaya salad), grilled corn, and fresh fruit (~200-350 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today — jet lag recovery is important. Apply sunscreen generously as October sun in Thailand can still be intense. October is the tail end of rainy season in some regions, so carry a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise beach walk. Join a morning snorkeling excursion departing from the resort beach or nearby pier. Explore colorful coral reefs and tropical fish in the clear coastal waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby island by longtail boat — enjoy a picnic-style lunch on the beach, swim in turquoise coves, and explore the island's interior jungle trails on foot. Many islands have stunning viewpoints reachable by a short hike.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the mainland by late afternoon. Shower and refresh at the resort, then head out for a relaxed beachfront dinner watching the sunset over the water.

meals.breakfast: Resort or nearby café — Thai-style breakfast with rice porridge (jok), fried eggs, and fresh juice (~150-250 THB)
meals.lunch: Packed snack box from resort or island beach shack — sandwiches, fruit, and water (~100-200 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachfront seafood restaurant — grilled whole fish with garlic and herbs, steamed rice, and cold Singha beer (~350-600 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Book snorkeling and island boat trips through your resort's concierge or reputable local tour operators. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a dry bag for valuables, and water shoes for rocky shores.

day_by_day.morning: Take a cooking class at a local Thai cooking school near the resort. Learn to make 3-4 classic dishes including Tom Kha Gai (coconut soup), Massaman curry, and spring rolls. Classes typically include a market visit to source fresh ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local fresh market to browse exotic tropical fruits, spices, and local produce. Pick up fresh rambutan, mangosteen, and dragon fruit to snack on. Explore any nearby temples or cultural landmarks within a short tuk-tuk ride.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Thai massage at a reputable spa near the resort (1-hour traditional massage ~400-600 THB). Afterwards, dine at a highly-rated local restaurant recommended by your cooking class instructor.

meals.breakfast: Cooking class typically includes breakfast or a light snack before the market tour (~included in class fee or ~150 THB separately)
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you cooked in class — a rewarding and authentic experience (included in cooking class fee ~800-1200 THB total)
meals.dinner: Mid-range Thai restaurant — try dishes outside your comfort zone like larb (spicy meat salad) or khao soi (northern curry noodle soup) (~300-500 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Book cooking classes at least a day in advance. Look for classes that include a market tour for the most immersive experience. Bring a notebook to record recipes to recreate at home.

day_by_day.morning: Island hopping day trip — depart early by speedboat to visit 3-4 smaller islands in the area. Snorkel at a vibrant coral reef, stop at a secluded white-sand beach, and explore sea caves or limestone karst formations by kayak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue island hopping — visit a famous viewpoint island for panoramic photos, swim in a natural lagoon, and relax on a pristine beach away from the crowds. Many tours include a seafood BBQ lunch on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and spend the evening exploring a local fishing village on foot — visit the pier at sunset to watch fishing boats return with the day's catch.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — grab pastries, fruit, and coffee to go (~150-200 THB)
meals.lunch: Seafood BBQ lunch included in island hopping tour — fresh grilled prawns, squid, and fish with rice (included in tour ~1500-2500 THB per person)
meals.dinner: Casual pier-side restaurant at the fishing village — fresh catch of the day prepared your choice of style (~300-500 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Book island hopping tours through your resort or a certified tour operator. Check weather forecasts the night before as speedboats may be cancelled in rough seas. Bring motion sickness tablets if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or hire a driver for a half-day exploration of the local area. Visit a Buddhist temple (wat) — dress modestly with shoulders and knees covered. Explore the temple grounds, observe monks' morning routines, and make a merit offering.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a songthaew (shared taxi) to a local waterfall or nature reserve for a refreshing swim and jungle walk. Many coastal Thai regions have beautiful inland waterfalls accessible within 30-60 minutes from beach resorts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beach area for a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar or beachside lounge. Afterwards, explore a local street food alley for dinner — try boat noodles, grilled pork skewers, and Thai iced tea.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or café near the temple — fresh baked goods, fruit smoothie (~100-200 THB)
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant near the waterfall — simple Thai rice dishes, stir-fried vegetables, and fresh coconut water (~150-250 THB)
meals.dinner: Street food alley dinner spread — multiple small dishes from different vendors (~200-350 THB)

day_by_day.notes: When visiting temples, always remove shoes before entering buildings, speak quietly, and never point feet toward Buddha images. Scooter rental is ~200-300 THB/day — ensure you have an international driving permit.

day_by_day.morning: Midpoint rest and leisure day. Sleep in, enjoy a long resort breakfast, and spend the morning lounging on the beach with a good book. Optional: try stand-up paddleboarding or kayaking along the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby town's main street and local market. Browse handicraft stalls for Thai silk scarves, handmade jewelry, and carved wooden souvenirs. Visit a local pharmacy or supermarket to restock any supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner at a well-regarded seafood or Thai fusion restaurant — a mid-trip treat. Enjoy fresh lobster, tiger prawns, or sea bass with a bottle of local wine or craft beer.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — enjoy everything on offer as a mid-trip treat (~200-350 THB)
meals.lunch: Market food court or casual café in town — try khao man gai (poached chicken rice) or pad see ew (~120-200 THB)
meals.dinner: Upscale-casual seafood restaurant — fresh catch, set menu or à la carte (~500-900 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a good day to do laundry at the resort or a local laundromat (~100-200 THB for a full load). Review the second half of your itinerary and confirm any remaining tour bookings.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise kayaking tour through mangrove forests — paddle through serene channels surrounded by ancient mangrove trees, spot exotic birds, and learn about the local ecosystem from a guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local elephant sanctuary (ethical — no riding) for a half-day experience. Feed, bathe, and walk with rescued elephants in a natural setting. Learn about elephant conservation efforts in Thailand.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a relaxing evening. Try a foot reflexology massage (~300-400 THB for 45 minutes) at a local massage parlor, then enjoy a quiet dinner near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before early kayaking tour — fruit, toast, and coffee (~100-150 THB)
meals.lunch: Elephant sanctuary typically provides a vegetarian Thai lunch (included in sanctuary fee ~1500-2500 THB)
meals.dinner: Cozy mid-range Thai restaurant near the resort — try panang curry or pineapple fried rice (~250-400 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Research and book only ethical elephant sanctuaries that do not offer riding. Wear clothes you don't mind getting wet or muddy at the sanctuary. Bring insect repellent for the mangrove kayaking tour.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry or speedboat to a more distant, less-visited island for a full day of exploration. Arrive early to beat the crowds and enjoy the pristine beaches in relative solitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island on foot or by rented bicycle. Discover hidden coves, snorkel over coral gardens, and hike to a clifftop viewpoint for dramatic ocean panoramas. Spend a few hours simply unwinding on the quietest beach you can find.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the last ferry back to the mainland. Stop for dinner at a popular local restaurant you've been meaning to try — ask your resort staff for their personal recommendations.

meals.breakfast: Resort grab-and-go breakfast before ferry departure — banana, boiled egg, yogurt (~100-150 THB)
meals.lunch: Island beach shack or bring a packed lunch — fresh coconut, grilled corn, and fruit (~150-250 THB)
meals.dinner: Staff-recommended local restaurant — try whatever the daily special is for an authentic experience (~250-450 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules carefully and note the last return time to avoid being stranded overnight. Bring sufficient cash as remote islands often don't have ATMs. Pack a full day bag with water, snacks, and sun protection.

day_by_day.morning: Join a local street food tour led by a food guide — walk through local neighborhoods, visit a wet market, and sample 8-10 different Thai dishes and snacks you might not find on tourist menus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local art gallery, cultural center, or historical museum to learn about the region's history, traditions, and relationship with the sea. Many coastal Thai towns have fascinating exhibits on fishing heritage and local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Thai cultural show if available locally — Muay Thai boxing matches, traditional dance performances, or a fire show on the beach are common evening entertainment options.

meals.breakfast: Street food tour typically begins with breakfast items — rice soup, Chinese-style doughnuts (patongo), and Thai tea (included in tour ~800-1200 THB)
meals.lunch: Continuation of street food tour or local restaurant discovered during the tour (~included or ~200-300 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachside restaurant with live music — enjoy a relaxed dinner with cocktails and ocean views (~350-600 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Street food tours are one of the best ways to eat adventurously and safely — guides know which vendors have the freshest ingredients. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Bring antacids just in case your stomach needs adjustment.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning fishing trip with local fishermen — experience traditional Thai fishing methods, help pull in nets, and enjoy the tranquility of the open sea at dawn. Many resorts or piers can arrange this experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a leisurely afternoon at the resort — use the pool, read, journal, or simply stare at the ocean. Optional: book a 90-minute resort spa treatment as a pre-departure treat (~600-1000 THB).
day_by_day.evening: Explore a different part of the beach strip you haven't visited yet. Browse boutique shops, try a new street food vendor, and pick up any last-minute gifts or souvenirs for friends and family.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before fishing trip — coffee, toast, fruit (~100-150 THB)
meals.lunch: Cook and eat your catch at a local restaurant that offers a 'cook your own catch' service, or enjoy a fresh seafood lunch near the pier (~300-500 THB)
meals.dinner: New area exploration — find a highly-reviewed local restaurant through Google Maps or TripAdvisor (~300-500 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Fishing trips depart very early (4-6 AM) so arrange a wake-up call. Bring layers as early morning on the water can be cool. This is a great opportunity for photography — the golden hour light on the sea is spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Final island or beach excursion — revisit your favorite beach or island from the trip for one last swim, snorkel, and relaxation session. Take final photos and soak in the beauty of the Thai coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort and begin packing. Do a final beach walk to collect any last shells or memories. Visit any shops you've been meaning to check out and complete souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best restaurant you discovered during your trip — celebrate the journey with your favorite Thai dishes, a toast with local Mekhong whiskey or Chang beer, and reflect on the highlights of your 13-day adventure.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — enjoy it fully one last time (~200-350 THB)
meals.lunch: Casual beach lunch — keep it light and simple, grilled fish or a noodle soup (~200-300 THB)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your trip's favorite restaurant — order generously and splurge a little (~500-800 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight details for the next day and arrange airport transfer in advance. Ensure all souvenirs are properly packed — check airline restrictions on items like fresh fruit, certain sauces, and liquids. Set a budget for last-minute airport shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand. Enjoy a slow last breakfast at the resort. Take one final walk on the beach at sunrise. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and arrange transfer to the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the airport with plenty of time (3 hours before international departure recommended). Complete check-in, immigration, and security. Browse duty-free shops for Thai snacks, jasmine rice, dried fruits, and Thai tea to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Board your departure flight. Carry happy memories, a full stomach of amazing Thai food, and a deep appreciation for the beauty, culture, and warmth of Thailand.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or nearby café — savor your last Thai breakfast (~150-250 THB)
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or food court — one last bowl of tom yum soup or pad thai (~200-350 THB)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight time and terminal the night before. Keep all receipts for VAT refund claims at the airport (Thailand offers VAT refunds on purchases over 2000 THB from participating stores). Leave a review for Aegean Bliss Resort and your favorite local experiences online to help future travelers.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in with welcome champagne and traditional Thai floral garland greeting. Settle into your beachfront suite and enjoy a late-night turndown service with complimentary fruit platter and herbal teas.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining from the resort's 24-hour menu — recommended: Tom Kha Gai soup and jasmine rice to ease into Thai flavors

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in preparation so your suite is fully ready upon late arrival. Keep the first night light — rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely start. Take a private sunrise beach walk along the resort's beachfront at your own pace. Indulge in a 90-minute traditional Thai herbal compress massage at the resort's luxury spa to recover from travel fatigue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation exploration of the immediate beach area. Rent a private longtail boat for a 2-hour scenic coastal cruise to discover nearby coves and hidden beaches. Snorkel in crystal-clear waters with premium gear provided by the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar. Stroll to the nearest local night market for an authentic street food introduction — sample satay skewers, mango sticky rice, and fresh coconut ice cream.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort's main restaurant featuring fresh tropical fruits, Thai congee, eggs benedict, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Light beach club lunch at the resort — grilled fresh catch of the day with papaya salad and coconut water
meals.dinner: Night market street food experience followed by a premium seafood dinner at a highly-rated beachside restaurant nearby — try whole grilled barramundi with garlic and chili

day_by_day.notes: October is transitional weather season in Thailand — pack light rain gear. The spa should be booked as soon as you check in to secure your preferred time slot.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private longtail boat excursion to a nearby uninhabited island for exclusive beach access. Enjoy a private picnic breakfast on the beach prepared by the resort's chef, complete with fresh fruit, pastries, and Thai iced coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Island snorkeling and free diving session with a certified private guide. Explore vibrant coral reefs and marine life. Return to the resort for a refreshing dip in the infinity pool overlooking the Andaman Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachfront dinner set up by the resort — tables on the sand with lanterns, personalized Thai tasting menu, and a dedicated butler service.

meals.breakfast: Private picnic breakfast on the uninhabited island — chef-prepared basket with tropical fruits, pastries, and Thai iced coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood BBQ on the island — grilled prawns, squid, and fish with Thai dipping sauces
meals.dinner: Exclusive private beachfront dining experience at the resort — 5-course Thai tasting menu featuring Massaman lamb, green curry, and coconut panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Book the private island excursion at least one day in advance through the resort concierge. Bring high-SPF sunscreen and reef-safe products to protect the coral ecosystem.

day_by_day.morning: Join a premium small-group Thai cooking class hosted by a local master chef. Learn to prepare 4 signature Thai dishes including Pad Thai, Tom Yum, green curry, and mango sticky rice using fresh market ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a vibrant local floating market or fresh produce market with a private guide. Sample exotic street foods — durian, rambutan, grilled corn, and fresh sugarcane juice. Shop for premium Thai spices, silk scarves, and handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset yoga session on the beach. Enjoy cocktails at the sky bar with panoramic ocean views before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-room Thai breakfast delivered to your terrace — rice porridge with century egg, fresh fruits, and Thai milk tea
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class
meals.dinner: Upscale Thai restaurant in town renowned for royal Thai cuisine — try Gaeng Panang and whole steamed sea bass in lime and garlic

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is typically a 4-hour experience — morning sessions are best before the heat peaks. Bring cash (Thai Baht) for market shopping as many vendors do not accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day island hopping adventure begins with an early departure on a private chartered speedboat. First stop: a stunning limestone karst island with emerald lagoons and sea caves — kayak through hidden hongs (inland lagoons).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue island hopping to a second island known for pristine white sand beaches. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch on the beach. Snorkel around coral gardens and spot tropical fish, sea turtles, and reef sharks.
day_by_day.evening: Final island stop for a breathtaking sunset before the speedboat returns to the resort. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxing evening at the resort's overwater lounge.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast box from the resort — sandwiches, fruit, granola bars, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the beach — charcuterie, fresh seafood, tropical fruits, and sparkling water prepared by the resort chef
meals.dinner: Resort's signature fine dining restaurant — Chef's special 7-course degustation menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Private speedboat charter for the full day is a premium experience — confirm booking 48 hours ahead. Bring motion sickness tablets if needed. Waterproof bags for electronics are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and lounge by the infinity pool. Optional: book a 2-hour couple's spa treatment featuring traditional Thai massage, hot stone therapy, and aromatic oil treatments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local beach town on foot or by private tuk-tuk. Discover hidden street food gems — pad see ew from a wok master, crispy pork belly over rice, and fresh-cut fruit cups. Visit a local Buddhist temple for cultural enrichment.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Thai cultural performance — classical dance show or Muay Thai exhibition at a local venue. Dinner at one of the area's most celebrated seafood restaurants on the pier.

meals.breakfast: Extended resort buffet breakfast — smoked salmon, dim sum, fresh juices, and made-to-order omelets
meals.lunch: Street food tour through town — budget around 4–5 different stalls for a diverse tasting experience
meals.dinner: Premium pier-side seafood restaurant — whole grilled lobster, oysters, and Thai seafood hot pot with premium Thai whisky

day_by_day.notes: When visiting temples, dress respectfully — cover shoulders and knees. Lightweight scarves are ideal. The resort can arrange a private tuk-tuk driver for the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise kayaking adventure through mangrove forests with a private naturalist guide. Discover diverse bird species, monitor lizards, and unique coastal ecosystems. Return for a refreshing outdoor shower and breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private yacht half-day charter — sail along the coastline, anchor at a secluded bay, swim, and sunbathe on deck. The yacht includes a crew, snorkeling equipment, and a stocked bar.
day_by_day.evening: Return from yacht at golden hour. Beachfront bonfire arranged by the resort with live acoustic Thai music, cocktails, and grilled satay. Wind down with a moonlit beach walk.

meals.breakfast: Post-kayaking resort breakfast — acai bowls, fresh coconut, avocado toast, and tropical smoothies
meals.lunch: On-board yacht lunch — fresh sashimi, cold noodle salads, and tropical fruits with chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Resort beachfront bonfire dinner — grilled whole fish, BBQ prawns, som tum salad, and sticky rice

day_by_day.notes: Mangrove kayaking is best done at high tide — confirm timing with the guide. The yacht charter can be arranged through the resort concierge or a reputable local charter company.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby larger island by private speedboat transfer. Morning hike to a scenic viewpoint offering panoramic 360-degree views of the surrounding islands and turquoise sea. Photography golden hour opportunity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island's famous beach — rent sun loungers and umbrellas at a premium beach club. Enjoy water sports: jet skiing, parasailing, or paddleboarding. Visit the island's lively beach market for street food snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return speedboat transfer to the resort. Evening at leisure — enjoy the resort's rooftop pool under the stars with cocktails and a cheese and charcuterie board.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast before early departure — fresh fruit, yogurt parfait, and strong Thai coffee
meals.lunch: Premium beach club lunch on the island — fresh grilled seafood platter, coconut curry, and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Resort's Thai-fusion restaurant — wagyu beef massaman, truffle tom kha, and lychee sorbet dessert

day_by_day.notes: Popular islands can be crowded — aim to arrive early (before 9:00 AM) to enjoy quieter moments at viewpoints and beaches. The resort concierge can recommend the best current beach clubs.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive ethical elephant sanctuary visit — spend the morning feeding, bathing, and walking with rescued elephants in a responsible, cage-free environment. Learn about elephant conservation from knowledgeable guides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a leisurely afternoon. Indulge in the resort's private beach cabana with personalized butler service — chilled towels, fresh juices, and afternoon canapés. Optional: resort's private pool villa upgrade for the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail masterclass at the resort bar — learn to craft signature Thai cocktails using lemongrass, kaffir lime, and galangal. Followed by a candlelit dinner at the resort's beachside restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before elephant sanctuary — light options: fruit, yogurt, and toast
meals.lunch: Traditional Thai home-cooked meal served at the elephant sanctuary — authentic rural flavors
meals.dinner: Candlelit beachside dinner at the resort — pan-seared red snapper, coconut jasmine rice, and warm pandan cake with vanilla ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Choose only ethical, reputable elephant sanctuaries that do not offer riding. The resort concierge can vet and book a certified ethical sanctuary. This experience requires a half-day departure — start early.

day_by_day.morning: Premium deep-sea fishing charter — head out to open waters with an experienced captain and crew. Try your hand at sport fishing for marlin, tuna, or mahi-mahi. The catch can be prepared by the resort's chef for dinner.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from fishing by early afternoon. Visit a nearby artisan village to observe traditional Thai silk weaving and wood carving. Purchase premium handmade gifts and authentic Thai crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Chef's table experience at the resort — watch the executive chef prepare a bespoke 6-course dinner using your fresh catch of the day combined with premium local ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Hearty resort breakfast before fishing — eggs, protein-rich dishes, fresh juice, and coffee
meals.lunch: On-boat packed lunch — sandwiches, chips, cold beverages, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Exclusive chef's table dinner at the resort — personalized 6-course menu featuring your fresh catch, complemented by Thai herbs and premium wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Deep-sea fishing charters typically depart very early (6:00–7:00 AM). Confirm seasickness precautions. The chef's table experience should be arranged at least 2 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Guided scuba diving excursion to a world-class dive site — explore underwater pinnacles, swim-throughs, and vibrant coral walls teeming with marine life including whale sharks (seasonal), rays, and moray eels. Suitable for certified and beginner divers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-dive relaxation at the resort's beach club. Enjoy a rejuvenating 60-minute deep tissue massage to soothe muscles after diving. Lounge by the pool with fresh coconut water and tropical snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell street food progressive dinner — guided tour of the best street food stalls in the local area, sampling 8–10 different dishes across multiple vendors. End the night with Thai desserts and fresh fruit shakes.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dive light breakfast — banana, toast, and energy drink to avoid discomfort underwater
meals.lunch: Post-dive recovery lunch at the resort beach club — protein-rich grilled chicken satay, rice, and fresh watermelon juice
meals.dinner: Progressive street food tour — pad thai, grilled skewers, fried rice, green papaya salad, mango sticky rice, and Thai iced tea across multiple street vendors

day_by_day.notes: Do not fly within 24 hours after scuba diving — plan accordingly if departure is approaching. Beginner divers should opt for a resort/discover scuba session rather than open water dives.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning island excursion — private longtail boat to a secluded secret beach for a quiet, exclusive last beach experience. Bring a book, snorkel gear, and enjoy the solitude of paradise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for final packing and leisurely farewell activities. Indulge in one last spa treatment — a 90-minute traditional Thai herbal ball massage and aromatherapy facial. Request a late checkout if available.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's premier restaurant — order from the à la carte premium menu featuring the best of Thai cuisine. Toast the trip with a bottle of fine champagne watching the last sunset over the ocean.

meals.breakfast: Special farewell breakfast in bed — full Thai and Western spread delivered to your terrace with fresh flowers
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — club sandwich, fresh salad, and tropical smoothie
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's premier restaurant — lobster bisque, red curry duck, and a decadent coconut and mango dessert tower with champagne

day_by_day.notes: Request late checkout (2:00–4:00 PM) to maximize the final day. Ensure all souvenirs, spices, and liquids are properly packed for air travel. Confirm transfer arrangements for the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach walk — take one last stroll along the beachfront to soak in the beauty of Thailand. Enjoy a quiet morning coffee on your terrace with ocean views. Complete final packing and checkout formalities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time: optional last-minute souvenir shopping in the local market for Thai snacks, silk products, and spices to bring home. Private luxury transfer to the airport with ample time for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Airport departure — relax in the premium lounge before your flight. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of beaches, island hopping, and world-class Thai cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — choose your favorites from the menu as a send-off meal
meals.lunch: Airport premium lounge dining or a final quick street food snack near the market
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details and ensure your private airport transfer is booked. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Declare any food items (dried fruits, packaged snacks) at customs. Keep a small amount of Thai Baht for last-minute purchases.
